title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an alleged misuse of law enforcement systems by an insider, not a failure of a model or an automated decision. The access that made it possible was legitimate: a deputy's credentials to databases and camera systems built for police work. The failure sits at the point where authorised access meets no check on purpose, and the reporting does not establish what logging, audit or supervisory review existed over those queries.

The systems named in the charges are a license plate data system and law enforcement databases and camera systems. Prohibited use of captured license plate data is charged as its own count, which indicates the data had a defined permitted purpose that the alleged conduct fell outside of. Catching this kind of use requires query auditing tied to case numbers or stated reasons, and review that compares access against actual investigations, not credentials alone.

What is not established is guilt. The eight counts are indictments returned by a grand jury, which is an accusation, not a finding, and no trial outcome appears in the reporting. The facts also do not establish how the alleged tracking was discovered or whether any system flagged it.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff’s deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, was released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including four counts of violation of oath by a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Prosecutors allege he misused law enforcement databases and camera systems for personal reasons between April and May 2024. The woman he is accused of tracking spoke anonymously, saying she hopes her story helps other women report abuse.

The Georgia Bureau of Investigation led the multi-year investigation, which began in 2024 after then-Sheriff Doyle Wooten requested it. Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled to appear for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
